forecast.

roads are impassable. Some evacuations occur in southern parts of

parts yard in Carthage is extensively flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours
ending at 12:30 PM EDT Thursday was 12.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage
just after midnight tonight and continue falling and remain
below flood stage.
- Flood stage is 7.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/ind.

The next statement should be issued late tonight by around 430 AM
EDT.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 13 at 1:47PM AKDT until August 14 at 4:30AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
Mendenhall Lake gauge levels, along with USGS imagery from Suicide
Basin and water levels within the basin, indicate that the release is
starting to slow its release of water into Mendenhall Lake and River.
Levels on the Mendenhall Lake and River will rise through this
afternoon as the release continues, with a forecast crest around 14.8
feet expected Thursday between 3pm to 4pm.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by a glacier-dammed lake outburst is
expected.

* WHERE...The Mendenhall Lake And River near the Mendenhall Glacier
Recreation area, View Drive and below Back Loop bridge.

* WHEN...Until 430 AM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the area around Mendenhall Lake and along the
Mendenhall River is ongoing. Water levels will start to slow before
beginning to fall through Thursday afternoon while water
temperatures in the lake and river will stay cold.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 500 AM AKDT, gauge data reported a glacier-dammed lake
outburst is ongoing. Flooding is ongoing near the Mendenhall Lake
And River.
- The outburst flood forecast is based on an estimated volume of
water in the glacier dammed lake and an estimated release rate
based on previous events. The extent of water drainage within the
basin (partial or full) can vary widely between outburst flood
events and is a major source of uncertainty in the forecast,
particularly with regard to the peak flood stage.
- For Mendenhall Lake :
At 1:15 pm the stage was 14.5 feet, in Major Flood Stage. Water
levels will go below major flood stage around 5:00pm Thursday.
Water levels will go below minor flood stage around 9:00pm
Thursday. A crest between 14.8 feet is expected between 3pm and
4pm Thursday.

At 13.0 feet: The low section of road past 9374 View Dr will be
flooded with 2 ft of water. Water begins to flow through some
backyards of homes on the northside of View Dr and flood low lying
areas. A few locations on View Dr will see depths of 1 to 2 feet of
water in homes.

At 14.0 feet: The low section of road past 9374 View Dr will be
significantly flooded and impassable. Water will begin to flow over
the road from water flowing behind homes on the north side of View
Dr. More homes along View Dr will begin to see moderate to major
flooding. Locations on River Rd with low river banks will begin to
see water approach driveways.

At 15.0 feet: Major flooding of multiple homes along View Dr. Water
will begin to approach a few homes along River Rd with low river
banks with possible flooding of driveways and 1 to 2 feet of water in
backyards. Up to 1 foot of water covering Riverside Dr at Tournure St
and Mendenhall River School.

deaths occur in vehicles.

and lower the time required to cause hypothermia.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued August 13 at 4:08PM MDT until August 13 at 4:30PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
At 408 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 5 miles west of
Arapahoe Park, or 12 miles southeast of Denver, moving east at 15
mph.

HAZARD...Ping pong ball size hail and 60 mph wind gusts.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...People and animals outdoors will be injured. Expect hail
damage to roofs, siding, windows, and vehicles. Expect wind
damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

Locations impacted include...
Southern Aurora, eastern Centennial, Parker, Greenwood Village,
Lone Tree, Arapahoe Park and Foxfield.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds and large
hail.

Tornadoes can develop quickly from severe thunderstorms. Seek shelter
immediately in an interior room on the lowest floor of a well-built
structure.

NWSheadline: SEVERE THUNDERSTORM WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 430 PM MDT FOR WESTERN ARAPAHOE AND DOUGLAS COUNTIES

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 13 at 4:00PM MDT until August 13 at 7:00PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
FFWBOU

The National Weather Service in Denver has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
East Central Jefferson County in central Colorado...
Northwestern Douglas County in northeastern Colorado...

* Until 700 PM MDT.

* At 400 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 3 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1.5 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, gulches,
roads, and poor drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
South Platte, Buffalo Creek and Foxton.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Last Resort Creek, Buffalo Creek, North Fork South Platte River,
Willow Creek, Bear Creek, Pine Creek, Spring Creek, West Bear
Creek, Indian Creek, South Platte River, Long Gulch and Shinglemill
Creek.
properties.instruction:
Move to higher ground now. Act quickly to protect your life.

Excessive runoff from this storm will cause flash flooding of small
creeks and streams, country roads, farmland along creeks, and other
low lying areas.
